miniProject.title: Versioned RPC with replayable faults and bounded work
miniProject.brief: Create `loglab`, the reduced data system carried through this track, in your chosen implementation language. Build a versioned framed RPC between processes on your machine, with deterministic correctness gates before timing runs and explicit boundaries for retries, identity and overload.
steps: Create `loglab` with `proto/`, `net/`, `clock/`, `member/`, `storage/`, `replica/`, `consensus/`, `shard/`, `txn/`, `stream/`, `ops/`, `spec/`, `history/`, `faults/`, `bench/`, `tests/` and `reports/`. Record unary and streaming state machines in `proto/`; check legal transitions against gRPC lifecycles and retain transition fixtures.

Build versioned length-prefixed framing and a delimited comparison parser. Keep split-header, split-body, coalesced and split-delimiter fixtures, pre-allocation and decompression limits, and checksum corruption tests; compare encodings and preserve a schema-evolution compatibility table checked against independent decoders, including unknown-field round trips.

Implement caller, incarnation, request and intent identities, atomic effect-plus-dedup transitions, parameter-mismatch rejection and bounded retention. Against a sequential intent model, test timeout windows, restart, remaining monotonic budgets, classified retries, jitter and token throttling; retain histories and a derived retry-amplification bound.

Add a token-issuing test client, authenticated channel and pre-dispatch authorization interceptor with a per-method policy table. Compare decisions with independent policy fixtures; inject stale discovery generations and keep denial, identity-propagation and versioned redirect traces proving rejected calls never mutate state.

Bound queues and connection checkout, add health-gated balancing, streaming half-close, flow control, cancellation propagation and drain. Check against a resource-ownership model; retain exhaustion and deadlock regressions plus cleanup traces, and explain the TCP versus QUIC transport boundary without implementing QUIC.

Cross client, server, schema and endpoint versions under deterministic delay, loss, duplication, reordering, partition, corruption, disconnect, restart and cancel schedules. Join traces by causal IDs, not timestamps; retain replay diffs, minimized failures, rollback verdicts and separate MIT 6.5840 Lab 2 and DSLabs Lab 1 results.

After correctness passes, compare shedding policies and affinity under repeated open-loop saturation and recovery runs. Check offered, admitted, rejected, retried and completed counts against raw histories; retain latency distributions, throughput, goodput, queue and pool occupancy, observer overhead, versions and workload descriptions.
deliverables: The `loglab` layout, versioned protocol, bounded RPC implementation and deterministic network with causal event histories.
Compatibility fixtures, independent state and policy checks, public-suite results, minimized regressions and rollout, rollback and idempotency contracts.
A measurement report rebuilt from repeated raw runs, with workload, versions, accounting boundaries and retained policy trade-offs.

checks.name: MIT 6.5840 Lab 2: Key/Value server and lock tests
checks.note: Keep reliable, unreliable and lock results separately; extend their ambiguity cases in your own matrix. Do not publish course solutions.

checks.name: DSLabs Lab 1: at-least-once and exactly-once RPC
checks.note: Retain Parts 2 and 3 search-test results; distinguish their sequential-client assumptions from your socket, restart and retention tests.

rubric.pass: Own framing and corruption tests match fixed byte fixtures; independent decoders confirm schema crossings and unknown-field behavior. Mixed-version rollback retains meaning and rejects incompatible requests.
rubric.strong: A planted field-reuse or lossy-proxy defect fails before repair; the minimized crossing remains a regression through rollback.

rubric.pass: Own histories match the sequential intent model across timeout windows, restarts, parameter conflicts and expiry. The contract names atomicity and retention limits; public-suite evidence is separate.
rubric.strong: A planted non-atomic dedup defect yields a minimized counterexample; delayed retries outside retention explicitly bound the guarantee.

rubric.pass: Independent policy fixtures and ownership assertions catch unauthorized dispatch, stale generations, leaks, unbounded checkout and stream deadlock. Cancellation and drain release owned resources without claiming effects were undone.
rubric.strong: Failures combined with discovery refresh or cancellation expose a naive fix; repaired transition-level regressions preserve rejection and cleanup evidence.

rubric.pass: Own replay tests reproduce raw histories exactly; causal joins ignore display timestamps. Repeated measurements follow correctness gates and reconcile counters with histories under named workloads and versions.
rubric.strong: A minimized fault and a losing policy regime survive the final report; observer overhead and queue-versus-service decomposition bound each performance claim.

miniProject.feedsInto: The protocol, bounded RPC, deterministic network, compatibility fixtures and causal histories feed identity, membership, storage, replication and consensus; the capstone inherits their contracts, replay evidence and measurement harness.
